A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Flow Map Matching work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original checkerboard simulations and image-generation results, including FID and Teacher-FID scores. Appendix D adds quantitative map-error analysis.

after.justification: V2 retains original simulation and image-generation results and adds a CIFAR-10 class-transfer demonstration in Section 4.2.1 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: V2 adds optional joint FMM/PFMM training with a single network and a stop-gradient multistep target (Section 3.7), plus class-switched backward/forward inference (Section 4.2.1). The principal distillation and direct-training objectives remain.

E1.justification: Checkerboard, CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-32 coverage remains. V2 adds an evaluated CIFAR-10 style-transfer task involving partial inversion and class switching, beyond v1's generation experiments and conceptual image-translation schematic.

E2.justification: Comparison membership is unchanged: Table 1 retains SI, EMD, LMD and PFMM; Table 2 retains DDPM and BatchOT against FMM; Figure 3 retains the same checkerboard methods. Newly cited consistency models are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added style-transfer evaluation specifies an eight-step map discretization, inversion to s'=0.3 and a subsequent class-label switch. Existing dataset sizes, training budgets and image-evaluation metrics remain unchanged, including Table 4.

E4.justification: Section 4.2.1 adds a qualitative case study of style preservation during class transfer, interpreted as evidence of cycle consistency. The earlier checkerboard coupling/error analysis is retained, with its visualization renumbered from Figure 5 to Figure 6.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The reporting practice and training-curve presentation remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 3 replaces the checkerboard KL results: for example, one-step FMM changes from 0.107 to 0.017 and SI from 0.020 to 0.016, now showing near parity. Figure 5 adds qualitative transfer results. Image scores in Tables 1-2 remain unchanged; unchanged Appendix Table 3 conflicts with the revised Figure 3, preventing an unqualified same-setting improvement claim.

T1.justification: New Appendix A supplies transport and stochastic-interpolant probability-flow proofs and derives the variance-preserving diffusion connection. V2 also formalizes Eulerian estimation in Proposition 3.12 with a proof, adds the diagonal boundary condition to Proposition 3.11 and revises the PFMM lemma's time grid. Much earlier theory is retained or relocated; the new Eulerian objective and its proof contain a sign inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces an unspecified sampling-cost reduction with an explicit 10-20-fold generation-time reduction at quality comparable to flow matching. The main claims about two-time maps, Lagrangian learning and unification of existing approaches remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains how inversion depth controls style preservation and interprets the transfer examples as demonstrating cycle consistency. Appendix A.4 also discusses eliminating finite-horizon diffusion bias. Earlier spatial-gradient failure explanations and stop-gradient stability caveats are largely retained or moved.

D1.justification: The Table 1 caption newly specifies adaptive fifth-order Runge-Kutta integration for the teacher, and Algorithms 1-3 make coupling/noise batch construction explicit. These are additional disclosures; Table 4's hyperparameters, hardware information and the implementation code pointer remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Generalized Consistency Trajectory Models and Bidirectional Consistency Models, explaining their relationship to stochastic interpolants, diffusion models and the Lagrangian approach. Existing research positioning is extended rather than replaced.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and methodological exposition are extensively rewritten. Section 3 introduces stochastic interpolants earlier and separates Eulerian estimation and progressive distillation; the appendices are reorganized and references move before them.

P2.justification: V2 adds style-transfer Figure 5, redraws checkerboard Figure 3, arranges Table 1 with step counts side by side, reformats the algorithms and enlarges Figure 4's legend. Most other displays retain their content, with relocations and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 provides clearer organization, a more self-contained mathematical foundation and a useful transfer demonstration. However, Figure 3's revised results now conflict broadly with unchanged Table 3, and the new Eulerian-estimation objective in Eq. (3.22) uses a minus sign where its proof in Eq. (B.24) uses a plus. These empirical and mathematical inconsistencies leave the net quality benefit uncertain.
